Final Report 
The Effect of Different Ratios of Earth Soil to Lunar Regolith on Different Types of Plants 
Team: LeMoon James 
Team # 23292 
Team Photo: 
 
 
Variables: 
 
●​ Independent Variable: different ratio of Earth soil to lunar regolith, type of plants 
 
●​ Dependent Variable:: how tall the plants will grow 
 
●​ Controls: plants were grown in 100% Earth soil to compare the experiment to. 
 
●​ Constants included pot size, amount of water given, amount of light 
 
Hypothesis: 
●​ The microgreens will grow best in 75% lunar soil. We think this because microgreens do not need much 
to grow. 
 
Background/Reasoning: 
●​ We chose the lunar regolith. Since the Artemis program is going to return astronauts to the moon next 
year, we should start studying how to grow plants on the moon. This will also help us as the moon will 
become a launching point for future missions to Mars. 
 
Rational Experiment: 
●​ Our experiment brings value to the scientific community because it shows if we can or cannot plant 
certain plants in lunar or martian soils. If we did not do this we would not be able to see what and what 
we can’t plant on the moon. This is important because as we colonize the moon we have to be able to 
have a food supply as we will not be able to transport all of our food in rockets. It will be too expensive 
and if we don't have fresh food we will be lacking nutrients.

Grow Pot Set Up: 
 
 
 
 
Procedures: 
Initial Planting Procedures 
●​ 1st step- Put the designated amounts of earth soil, amendments, and lunar regolith in a cup. 
●​ 2nd step- Mix them all together. 
●​ 3rd step- Put paper towels at the bottom of the pot. 
●​ 4th step- Pour the cup of soil/regolith/amendment mixture into the pot 
●​ 5th step- Plant the seeds (10 seeds) 2 cm deep in the soil 
●​ 6th step- Add 100ml of water to the pot 
●​ 7th step- Let it sit.

Weekly Measuring/Watering/Picture Procedures 
●​ 1st step-Take a picture of the progress 
●​ 2nd step-Add pictures to the pictures document 
●​ 3rd step-Measure the tallest plant in the pot in centimeters 
●​ 4th step-Then fill up a graduated cylinder with 100 ml of water 
●​ 5th step- Pour the water into the pot gently 
●​ 6th step- Put the tray in the light to grow 
●​ 7th step- Let it sit and absorb the water 
●​ 8th step- Repeat each Monday.

Analysis 
●
The plants did the best in the earth’s soil. I think some of the plants did not grow as much because they
probably were not all planted at the same level; they were either too high or too low into the soil.
Lettuce grew the most out of all of the plants.
●
Some conclusions about the experiment were good overall. However, some of the things that we could
have done differently could be when we planted the seeds we should have planted them deeper. The
data that we collected all together from each of the plants could have been better, because in the data
collection chart it shows basil went from .2 to .2 to 0 to 3.1 and then back to 0. So the plants could have
died but when I saw on the data chart .2 to 0 to 3.1, It doesn’t make sense because that means the
plant died and then came back to life in 1 day somehow.
Future Considerations 
●
Some changes we could have made to improve our experiment were: using different water
measurements, changing the type of plants, or the type of amendments we used. We also could have
changed the amount of sunlight, and mixed the different soil mixture together better.
Conclusions 
●
Our experiment showed that different mixes of Earth soil and lunar regolith changed how tall the
microgreens grew. We learned that plants can grow in lunar regolith if we add nutrients, but they usually
did better when there was some Earth soil mixed in. This is important because this type of research can
help future astronauts grow plants on the moon. The coolest thing we learned was that lettuce grew
quickly and also died quickly.
